concept.title: Signing in
concept.shortdesc: Open the app in your browser and you land on the sign-in screen.

ul.li: Sign in with your email and password.
Create a new account switches the form to registration: enter your name, email, and a password (minimum 8 characters).
Sign in with Google appears when the server has been configured with a Google OAuth client. If it is not configured, a note on the sign-in screen says so.

Already have a password account? Signing in with Google (or your server's single sign-on) at the same address brings you back to the sign-in screen, which asks for that account's password once. Enter it and Google is connected: from then on either one signs you in to the same account. The password is what proves the account is yours, so an account made with Google or single sign-on cannot be joined to another provider this way.

conbody.p: Some servers sign everyone in through single sign-on only (on openv.app, that is DMSid, the one login for every DMS SaaS product). There the sign-in screen has no form and no buttons: opening it, or any Sign up or Create free account link, takes you straight to the provider's own sign-in or sign-up page and brings you back signed in. After you sign out, or if signing in did not finish, the screen stays put with a button to continue or Try again, and says what happened: that you cancelled at the provider, that the provider has not confirmed your address, or that the sign-in did not complete. An account you made earlier with a password is still yours: the first time you sign in through the provider at the same address, OpenV asks for that account's password once to connect the two, and from then on the provider signs you in. If you no longer know that password, Forgot your OpenV password? on the same screen emails you a link to set a new one (see Forgot your password? below); setting it does not sign you in, it lets you finish connecting. An invitation link names the workspace and the address it was sent to; continue to the provider and sign in with that address to join. To sign in once connected, use the provider's own password and its own reset.
The first user to register becomes the server admin.

After signing in you are taken to the Projects page. On a server that sends email, a new account first sees a Check your inbox page: click the link in the email (valid for 24 hours) and you are through. The page can resend the email, send it to a corrected address, or sign you out.

Some servers close registration: there is then no Create a new account button, and the sign-in screen tells you to ask a workspace admin for an invitation. The invitation link is the way in — it opens the sign-up form with your address already filled in, and joins you to the workspace that invited you. Use the link itself, whether you are creating an account or signing in to one you already have; typing the invited address into a sign-up form without the link joins nothing, and on a closed server does not let you sign up at all. If you are already signed in when you open the link, OpenV shows you the invitation and you press Join — and if you are signed in as a different address, it says which address to sign in as instead. Single sign-on is unaffected: an invited address joins its workspaces as it signs in, because the identity provider vouches for the address.

section.title: Your password and your sessions
section.p: Open your settings from the user block at the bottom-left of the sidebar to change your password — current password, then the new one twice. Changing it signs out every other browser and device you are signed in on, which is what you want if you are changing it because the old one may have leaked; the browser you are using stays signed in. Accounts that sign in with Google or single sign-on have no password here — change it at that provider.

section.title: Forgot your password?
section.p: On the sign-in screen, Forgot your password? asks for the address you sign in with and emails it a link to set a new password. The link works once and expires after an hour; the page says the same thing whether or not the address has an account, so it cannot be used to find out who has one. Setting the new password signs the account out everywhere, and you sign in again with it. If nothing arrives, check the address and your spam folder.

On a server that cannot send email the screen says so, and the way in is your OpenV administrator: a platform admin can make a reset link for your account (see the Platform admin chapter) and pass it to you. That link lasts a day and works once.
Accounts that sign in with Google or single sign-on have no password to reset — sign in there.

On a server that signs everyone in through single sign-on only, the reset is for one thing: connecting the provider to an account you made earlier with a password. Setting the new password does not sign you in and does not bring the password form back. The screen says your password is set; continue to the provider, and enter the new password when OpenV asks for it.

section.title: Removing your account
section.p: On a server that signs people in with DMSid, your DMSid page lists the products you can be removed from. Remove my account from OpenV (and Delete my DMSid, which removes you from every product first) ends your OpenV account:

ul.li: You are signed out everywhere, and your runner keys, connected AI apps, notifications, workspace memberships and pending invitations go.
A workspace only you belong to, your personal one among them, is deleted with everything in it.

What you wrote in workspaces other people use — requirements, links, comments, test results, baselines — stays for them, shown as written by Deleted user. Nothing left there names you or your address.

section.p: Two things stop it, and DMSid shows you which, with nothing removed: being the only admin of a workspace that has other members (make someone else an admin, or remove the others, first), and a workspace that only you belong to still having a paid subscription (cancel it in the workspace's billing settings first). Signing in with DMSid again afterwards starts a new, empty OpenV account.

Sessions do not last forever: one expires a set time after you sign in, and sooner if you stop using it. Your server's administrator sets both limits (30 days and 7 days unless they shortened them), and you simply sign in again.
